exactText: If I had to predict what will in retrospect be the most important new technology of the 2020s, it would be hard to choose between AI and fusion. Both will change everything.
sourceQuote: the most important new technology of the 2020s, it would be hard to choose between AI and fusion.
normalizedClaim: AI or fusion (or both) will be retrospectively judged the most important new technology of the 2020s.
resolutionCriteria: Consensus among major technology historians, media retrospectives, or economic impact analyses (e.g., GDP contribution or citation metrics) by 2030 identifying AI and/or commercial fusion as the dominant technological advance of the decade.

exactText: he predicts inference prices will keep falling roughly 30x per year, keeping the lean model viable.
sourceQuote: inference prices will keep falling roughly 30x per year
normalizedClaim: AI inference prices continue falling at roughly 30x per year (at constant quality).
resolutionCriteria: Public pricing data from major AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) showing approximate 30x annual cost reduction for equivalent inference quality over the subsequent 2–3 years.

exactText: The biggest opportunity for would-be startup founders is AI. But the most underpriced opportunity is probably non-AI ideas. So if you have a good non-AI idea, go for it, because everyone else is going to overlook it.
sourceQuote: the most underpriced opportunity is probably non-AI ideas. So if you have a good non-AI idea, go for it, because everyone else is going to overlook it.
normalizedClaim: Non-AI startup ideas are currently underpriced relative to AI ideas and will produce outsized returns for founders who pursue them.
resolutionCriteria: YC or broader venture data showing that a meaningful share of the highest-returning startups founded in 2026–2028 are non-AI companies, or valuation multiples for non-AI startups rising relative to AI peers.

exactText: AI will be especially fatal to writing that takes too long to get to the point. Now there will always be a more concise alternative, and 99% of readers will choose it.
sourceQuote: AI will be especially fatal to writing that takes too long to get to the point. Now there will always be a more concise alternative, and 99% of readers will choose it.
normalizedClaim: AI summarization and concise alternatives will cause the large majority of readers to abandon long-winded writing.
resolutionCriteria: Measurable decline in engagement metrics (time-on-page, completion rates) for long-form non-fiction writing versus AI-generated concise versions, as reported by major publishers or analytics platforms by 2028.

exactText: When I was a kid I didn't realize, as is now obvious, that AGI would be a wide band rather than a sharp finish line. But if you'd shown me a version of ChatGPT that had been told to act like a human, I'd definitely have said that AI had been achieved.
sourceQuote: AGI would be a wide band rather than a sharp finish line.
normalizedClaim: AGI will prove to be a continuum/wide band of capabilities rather than a single discrete threshold event.
resolutionCriteria: Consensus statements from leading AI labs and researchers by 2030 describing AGI as a gradual spectrum rather than a binary achievement.

exactText: founders in the future "will look exactly like they did 20 years ago, not like robots."
sourceQuote: founders in the future "will look exactly like they did 20 years ago, not like robots."
normalizedClaim: Successful startup founders in the coming years will continue to exhibit the same human traits (formidability, speed, fear of failure) as those of the mid-2000s rather than becoming primarily AI-augmented or robot-like.
resolutionCriteria: Qualitative and quantitative analysis of YC and top-tier startup founder profiles in 2030 showing continuity of human characteristics rather than dominance by AI-native or fully automated founding processes.

exactText: The best predictor of success for tech companies, at every stage from during the YC batch to public company with billions in revenue, is the rate of shipping new stuff.
sourceQuote: The best predictor of success for tech companies, at every stage from during the YC batch to public company with billions in revenue, is the rate of shipping new stuff.
normalizedClaim: Shipping velocity remains the strongest predictor of tech company success across all stages.
resolutionCriteria: Empirical studies or YC/venture data through 2029 correlating feature-release frequency with valuation growth, survival, or exit outcomes, confirming it as the top predictor.

exactText: AI may finally allow us to test whether (or more precisely where) you make more money by being good. In startups you generally do, which is one reason I like this world.
sourceQuote: In startups you generally do, which is one reason I like this world.
normalizedClaim: In the startup domain, ethical behavior correlates with higher financial returns, and AI will enable clearer testing of this relationship.
resolutionCriteria: Controlled studies or large-scale data (enabled by AI evaluation tools) by 2030 showing positive correlation between ethical metrics and startup financial outcomes.

exactText: There's a startup in the current YC batch that's growing at 57% a week. And not because they started last week; they've been doing this for a couple months. They can't keep growing at this rate for too many more months; you run out of atoms; but they're likely to be big.
normalizedClaim: The specific YC S26 (or current 2026) startup growing at 57% weekly will become a large successful company.
resolutionCriteria: Public disclosure or YC follow-up reporting that the identified high-growth startup reaches unicorn status or significant scale (e.g., >$100M ARR or major acquisition) within 3–5 years.

exactText: The biggest opportunity for would-be startup founders is AI.
sourceQuote: The biggest opportunity for would-be startup founders is AI.
normalizedClaim: AI represents the single largest opportunity category for new startup founders as of 2026.
resolutionCriteria: Venture capital deployment data and YC batch composition for 2026–2028 showing AI startups receiving the plurality or majority of early-stage funding and producing the highest number of breakout companies.
